chunks: Al-Kafi: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Sahl ibn Ziyad, all together, from Ibn Mahbub from Jamil ibn Salih, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Learn the Qur'an, for it will come on the Day of Judgment to its companion in the form of a handsome, pale-faced youth. The Qur'an will say to him: I am the one who kept awake your nights, made thirsty your mid-days, dried your saliva, and caused your tears to flow. I will accompany you wherever you recite, and just as every merchant is behind his merchandise (seeking profit), so am I today behind you, the merchant of every merchant. An honour will come to you from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, so receive glad tidings.' Then a crown will be brought and placed on his head, and he will be given the Writ of Security in his right hand and the Writ of Eternity in the Gardens in his left hand, and he will be attired with two robes. Then it will be said to him: 'Recite and ascend!' So every time he recites a verse, he ascends a level. And his two parents will be attired with two robes if they were believers, then it will be said to them: 'This is for what you taught him the Qur'an.'
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for learning and reciting the Qur'an on the Day of Judgment according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from Al-Kafi emphasizes the Qur'an as a living intercessor, personified as a handsome youth who validates the believer's sacrifices of sleep and thirst. It underscores the tangible eschatological rewards, including the crown of honor and the elevation of parents, linking the spiritual discipline of recitation directly to divine mercy and familial honor.
